chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said regarding a hunt in which an arrow was found, and it was dead, not known who killed it: 'Do not eat it.'

key_terms.لَا تَطْعَمْهُ: do not eat it — the ruling (hukm)
key_terms.لَا يُدْرَى مَنْ قَتَلَهُ: not known who killed it — the crucial element establishing legal uncertainty

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating game found dead with an arrow when it is unknown who killed it?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) narrates that Imam Ali (peace be upon him) ruled that if a hunted animal is found dead with an arrow in it, but it is unknown who shot the arrow that killed it, the animal may not be consumed. This ruling is rooted in the Islamic principle that the lawfulness of slaughtered or hunted meat requires certainty that it was killed in the prescribed manner (by a Muslim who invoked God's name). Since the identity of the hunter — and therefore whether proper conditions were met — is unknown, caution mandates abstaining from the meat.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said regarding a hunt in which an arrow was found, and it was dead, not known who killed it. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not consume it’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn abu Najran from ‘Asem ibn Hamid from Muhammad ibn Qays who has said the following: “Abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
’Amir al-Mu’minin, about a prey that is found dead with an arrow in it and it is not known who has killed it, said, ’Do not use it for food.’”
